merge.name: summary-renders
merge.note: A summary alone. Counts as given; self from self_reactor.

merge.name: stale-update-dropped
merge.note: Version 6 is below the held 7, so it is an update the summary already folded in.

merge.name: equal-version-dropped
merge.note: Accept strictly greater. The same version is the same state.

merge.name: newer-update-applied
merge.note: Count comes from the update, not from adding one: an update is state, not a delta.

merge.name: update-to-zero-removes-pill
merge.note: Zero count, no pill.

merge.name: tombstone-rejects-late-add
merge.note: The server keeps an emptied emoji's version, so the client must too. Without the tombstone the late ADDED at 3 would resurrect the pill.

merge.name: readd-after-empty
merge.note: A re-add comes above the tombstone and is accepted.

merge.name: new-emoji-from-stream
merge.note: An emoji we have never held has no watermark; any version is accepted. Equal counts fall back to UTF-8 byte order: 🎉 (F0 9F 8E 89) before 👍 (F0 9F 91 8D).

merge.name: own-update-from-another-device
merge.note: Our own reaction made on another device arrives on the stream and highlights the pill.

merge.name: tap-adds-optimistically
merge.note: The pill changes before the server answers, and is marked pending.

merge.name: tap-new-emoji
merge.note: Tapping an emoji the message does not have yet, from the strip or picker.

merge.name: tap-confirmed
merge.note: The response's EmojiReaction replaces the pending state.

merge.name: tap-removes
merge.note: Tapping a highlighted pill removes.

merge.name: remove-last-reaction
merge.note: Removing the only reaction hides the pill immediately, before the response.

merge.name: stream-during-pending-keeps-highlight
merge.note: Someone else's reaction lands while ours is on the wire: their count shows, our highlight stays.

merge.name: own-echo-before-response
merge.note: The stream can deliver our own add before the RPC returns. It must not count us twice (3), and the response at the same version is then a no-op.

merge.name: coalesce-on-off-on
merge.note: Three taps while the first add is in flight: one call. The later taps only move the displayed state.

merge.name: coalesce-on-off-then-settle
merge.note: On, then off, while the add is in flight. The add lands; the final state (off) differs from the server's (on), so a remove follows, and the pill shows the off state as pending until it returns.

merge.name: coalesce-on-off-on-settle
merge.note: On, off, on. The add lands and the final state already matches, so nothing more is sent.

merge.name: network-failure-rolls-back
merge.note: Back to the confirmed state, with the generic error.

merge.name: denied-rolls-back
merge.note: DENIED is shown like a network failure; the catalog should make it rare.

merge.name: too-many-types
merge.note: The 21st distinct emoji on a message.

merge.name: message-not-found-is-silent
merge.note: The message was deleted; the stream is removing it, so no error is shown.

merge.name: cannot-react-is-silent
merge.note: The strip should not have been offered. Roll back quietly.

merge.name: failure-drops-coalesced-taps
merge.note: Nothing is queued: a failure discards the taps made while it was in flight too.

merge.name: summary-omits-emptied-emoji
merge.note: A later summary without 👍 means it emptied.

merge.name: summary-keeps-pending-emoji
merge.note: A summary fetched before our add landed must not wipe the pending tap.

merge.name: reactions-are-per-emoji
merge.note: Versions are per (message, emoji). 🔥 at 3 is fresh even though 👍 is at 9.

order.name: count-descending
order.note: Phase 1: every boost total is 0, so count decides.

order.name: boost-before-count
order.note: Phase 2: any boost outranks any count. The unit is opaque here, only its order matters.

order.name: tie-on-utf8-bytes
order.note: Ties fall back to the server's order, UTF-8 byte order. ❤️ starts E2, the others F0.

order.name: tie-utf8-not-utf16
order.note: The case that separates byte order from a platform's default string compare. Both start U+261D. Next, ☝️ has U+FE0F (UTF-8 EF B8 8F) and ☝🏻 has U+1F3FB (F0 9F 8F BB): EF < F0 in UTF-8, but in UTF-16 the surrogate D83C < FE0F, which would flip them.

settle.name: first-render-is-target-order
settle.note: A row coming on screen shows `order` exactly, UTF-8 tiebreak included. Settling only governs changes after that.

settle.name: counts-live-positions-on-the-beat
settle.note: 🔥 shows 7 from 300 ms, but moves only on the first beat, 1000 ms after the last one.

settle.name: climb-three-places-per-beat
settle.note: A boost puts 🔥 first in `order`. It climbs three places per beat, so the climb is visible and each move is next door.

settle.name: top-inversion-first
settle.note: Two pairs are out of order and the beat allows one swap: the pair nearer the top goes first.

settle.name: touch-holds-the-row
settle.note: A touch at 900 ms holds the row until 2400 ms. The beat due at 1000 ms waits for it.

settle.name: hold-is-capped
settle.note: Each touch extends the hold, but not past 4000 ms from the touch that began it (500 ms). Someone tapping every second cannot freeze the row.

settle.name: new-hold-after-a-gap
settle.note: The first hold ends at 1600 ms, so the touch at 1600 ms begins a new one rather than extending the old one.

settle.name: no-swap-back-inside-cooldown
settle.note: 🔥 and 😂 swapped at 1000 ms, so they cannot swap back until 4000 ms, whatever the counts do.

settle.name: count-margin
settle.note: With a margin of 2, a lead of 1 is not enough to pass. The shipped value is 1; this pins the knob for anyone who changes it.

settle.name: money-ignores-count-margin
settle.note: Any boost lead passes, the smallest one included.

settle.name: live-tie-keeps-place
settle.note: Back to a tie, 😂 stays ahead of 🔥 on screen although `order` puts 🔥 first. The UTF-8 tiebreak decides where pills start, never a move.

settle.name: emptied-pill-waits-for-the-beat
settle.note: 👍 shows 0 in place until the beat, so the pills after it do not slide early.

settle.name: new-emoji-joins-at-the-end
settle.note: A new emoji appears on the beat, after the last pill, where it moves nothing but the "+" pill.

settle.name: new-boosted-emoji-climbs
settle.note: It joins at the end and spends that beat's three swaps climbing, then climbs on.

settle.name: tap-grace-hits-the-old-layout
settle.note: A thumb already on its way to 😂 in the first slot still gets 😂 for 450 ms after the swap. Slot 2 is the "+" pill in both layouts.

settle.name: tap-grace-covers-the-plus-pill
settle.note: A joining emoji takes the "+" pill's place, so a tap there during the grace still opens the picker.

strip.name: reacted-with-a-recent
strip.note: A reaction already in the recents is highlighted in place, not moved.

strip.name: reacted-outside-recents
strip.note: After the six, next to +. The WhatsApp screenshot in the design review.

strip.name: several-outside-newest-first
strip.note: Newest reaction first, so the one you just made is the one visible before scrolling.

strip.name: mixed
strip.note: Only the reaction outside the recents is appended.

recents.name: empty-pads-defaults
recents.note: Nothing used yet: the defaults from node 10286:2573, in their order.

recents.name: frequency-first
recents.note: Most used first, then padding with the defaults.

recents.name: recency-breaks-ties
recents.note: Equal counts: most recently used first.

recents.name: padding-skips-used-defaults
recents.note: A default already ranked is not repeated.

recents.name: undrawable-skipped
recents.note: Emoji this device cannot draw are not offered, even if used on another OS version.

recents.name: picker-row-of-seven
recents.note: The picker asks for 7 and there are 6 defaults, so an unused picker shows 6. Not padded further: the row is not worth an invented seventh default.

recents.name: limit-truncates
recents.note: All used once, so recency orders them and the oldest two drop.

drawability.note: Mixed-skin-tone ZWJ sequence, Emoji 12.1. The case a glyph-count rule gets wrong on iOS.
Not an RGI sequence, so no font has a ligature; it draws as two emoji.
Regional indicators that are not a flag draw as two letters.
